filters: any sector/model: B2B, B2C, consumer, service, product — nothing pre-excluded
positive EBITDA ASAP (primary constraint — cash flow is the only gate)
evaluate purely on cash-flow fit: NO positive or negative bias toward tech, web3, or startup ideas
~1 Cr INR entry, growing from there
no category is pre-filtered; unfashionable/unexploited niches are preferred but not exclusive

opportunities.title: Commercial Kitchen Exhaust (Hood) Cleaning Service
opportunities.idea: Deep-clean grease from commercial kitchen exhaust hoods, ducts & fans for restaurants, hotels, cafeterias, cloud kitchens in Mumbai/Bangalore. Compliance-mandated recurring service.

findings: Proven recurring B2B service. Legal requirement for all commercial kitchens. Net margins 25-40%, startup ~Rs5-15L. Real casedata: 30 accounts = 60K USD/yr in 60 days. India providers exist in Mumbai (OXY, Accordible) & Bangalore (deepcleaning.in, EPSCO).
sources: YT: Austin Davis real case study; MFS Trade School; Phil Ackland Training; linkup: tradeindia, indiamart, market reports

opportunities.title: Water tanker / bulk water supply for housing societies & construction sites
opportunities.idea: Water tanker / bulk water supply for housing societies & construction sites

findings: Structural, recurring demand: Mumbai private tankers supply ~550 MLD daily via 2000-2500 vehicles; societies pay Rs 1-2L/month (medium) to Rs 10L/month (large complexes); Panvel medium societies spend Rs 8L/yr, larger up to Rs 20L. Non-potable (construction, hotels, gardens) + potable both large. Investable wedge is NOT owning a fleet (regulatory/stigma heavy, CGWA NOCs, BMC permits, Bengaluru registration needed) but a compliant asset-light broker/dispatcher + treated-STP-water-for-construction platform: verified tanker partners, subscription monthly-minimum contracts, booking/ETA/proof-of-delivery software, take-rate. Entry Rs 5-15L asset-light vs Rs 25-60L per owned 10KL vehicle. Unit economics one 10KL tanker @ 4.5 loads/day Rs 2700/load = ~Rs 3.16L/month revenue, ~29% EBITDA margin base case; strong dense-route 25-40%. ~1 Cr funds 2-3 vehicles OR a full broker platform. Watch-outs: CGA/BMC regulatory instability (June 2026 strike over CGWA NOCs), tanker-mafia stigma, drought-crisis pricing must NOT be underwritten as base case, receivables stretch 30-45 days.

opportunities.title: Commercial Linen & Uniform Rental for Hotels & Salons
opportunities.idea: Centralized commercial laundry facility providing linen & uniform rental + daily pickup/delivery to boutique hotels, gyms, clinics, and salon chains in MMR/Bangalore on monthly retainer.

findings: Market: India laundry & dry-cleaning ~Rs12,500cr FY26, Rs34,068cr by 2032; hotel linen infra underdeveloped, most smaller hotels in-house. Model: processing-only first (low WC) then rental for contracted accounts (3-par, min-billing, shrink/damage, deposit). Rental converts customer linen+capex+laundry into per-room/per-kg recurring contracted fee. Unit economics: gross 35-55%, EBITDA 10-18% (15-25% mature), break-even 18-30 months. Capital: lean pilot Rs35-70L (300-700kg/day), pro city cluster Rs1-2.5Cr (1-3 t/day). Providers: Mumbai - Relaef (Rs39/bed), The Laundry Bag, Washex (35+ sites), Fabricare; Bengaluru - LinenGrass (RFID), Relaef, Spin & Dry, Namma Dhobi. Winning wedge: one vertical + one geography micro-market (3-5 star independent hotels + serviced apartments, or restaurants/salons/spas).

opportunities.title: Elevator & Lift Maintenance AMC Service
opportunities.idea: Third-party non-OEM maintenance contracts for mid-rise residential apartments & commercial spaces across Bangalore/Mumbai, competing against expensive OEM AMCs.

findings: Boring recurring-revenue vertical. India installs 70-80k lifts/yr, growing serviceable base; OEMs dominate install (KONE,TK Elevator,Otis) but independents service ~50% of global units. Entry wedge: 8-20yr-out-of-warranty mid-market residential/commercial in one dense Mumbai/Bangalore cluster. Non-comprehensive AMC pricing: Rs15-30k/lift/yr basic, Rs25-50k standard, Rs35-80k+ comprehensive. Blended first-year revenue Rs32-50k/lift/yr; 15-25% EBITDA at 300-800 units, subscale <100-150 units is breakeven to 10%. 500 contracted lifts at Rs30k = Rs1.5 Cr recurring AMC revenue. Entry cost Rs60L-Rs1.5Cr credible city launch. Moat = technician density, response reputation, parts access, society trust, not software. Core diligence risk: recruit ex-OEM field supervisor + 2-4 technicians and win 150+ clustered units without destructive pricing. Compete on 2-4hr local response + digital logs, not price. Regulation: Maharashtra lift Act mandates annual license/inspection.

opportunities.title: B2B Pest Control & FSSAI Hygiene Audit Compliance
opportunities.idea: Quarterly pest eradication & mandatory FSSAI food-safety hygiene documentation for cloud kitchens, QSR chains, food processing units, and school canteens.

findings: India pest control market: USD 1.92B (2025) growing 5.82% CAGR to USD 3.3B by 2034 (IMARC); B2B = 75%+ of market. FSSAI Schedule 4 makes pest control + documented FSMS MANDATORY for every licensed food business (restaurants, cloud kitchens, hotels, food factories, central kitchens) - structural recurring demand, not discretionary. Best wedge: FSSAI-ready pest-compliance managed service for food businesses in one dense micro-market (Andheri-BKC-Powai / Koramangala-HSR-Bellandur). Revenue = annual 12-month AMC, quarterly advance billing. Unit economics: compliance-led AMC at INR 8,000-20,000/site/month, gross margin 60-75%, mature EBITDA 15-25% after route density (70-85% recurring revenue, 80-90%+ renewals). Food factory/central kitchen tickets INR 2-12L/yr are best ACV. Startup capital: INR 20-30L focused city launch (3-6 technicians, supervisor, vehicles, field app, 6-9mo runway) - fits 1Cr budget scaling from there. Moat = operational density + compliance data (QR-linked site records, device maps, digital reports, audit packs), not the chemical. Packaging as compliance/operational-risk tier (Core/Compliance/Assured) avoids competing on low-cost spray price. NRI-return founder fit: excellent - relationship-heavy B2B sales, no frontier tech, no web3. Watch-outs: insecticide licensing (state Insecticides Act/Rules, fumigation extra permits), low entry barriers + 15,000 unorganized players = price pressure; avoid hiring ahead of revenue & distant micro-accounts (kills EBITDA); route density is the key economic variable.

opportunities.title: Medical Equipment Rental & Home ICU Support
opportunities.idea: Rental of oxygen concentrators, hospital beds, BiPAP machines, and patient monitors to nursing homes and home-care patients in Tier-1 suburbs with monthly billing.

findings: Market: India home healthcare USD6.4B (2025)->USD16.8B (2033) 12.9% CAGR; DME market USD7.48B->11.69B 5.08% CAGR; global medical equipment rental USD65B->99B 5.4% CAGR. City-level sizing: 100-device respiratory fleet @65-75% util = Rs30-55L/yr; 250-350-device fleet + beds/monitors = Rs1.5-3Cr/yr one metro. Pricing Mumbai: 5L conc Rs2,850-3,490/mo, BiPAP Rs3,450-3,850, 10L Rs6,490-6,650. Bangalore: 5L Rs3,500 (Oxyease), BiPAP Rs3,900-5,000 (Okto), home vent from Rs25,000/mo. Payback 16-36 months by asset class. Demand drivers: post-ICU discharge, COPD/sleep/respiratory, palliative, 140M+ Indians aged 60+. Reference EBITDA: Portea -6.88%, Emoha -48.86% (platform trap); a lean local depot targets 10-15% mature EBITDA. Competition: Portea, Nightingales, Okto, Oxyease, Prime Healers, HDU, Medify (Mumbai/Bangalore). Recommended entry: focus 3-5 hospital/pulmonologist referral relationships, respiratory/COPD vertical, 2-hr delivery + backup-replacement SLA, B2B2C to hospitals/nursing agencies/insurers; sequence: concentrators/BiPAP/beds first, add ventilators after utilization + clinical SOP proven.
